help_heading: How companies make it into your strategy
help_intro: You set the rules. Each month, we apply them to the same companies and the same scores for everyone. Here is each step, including what AI does and what the code does.
help_step_1_text: On the last trading day of each month, we take a snapshot of about 3,000 U.S. companies and their data. Every strategy starts from that same snapshot.
help_step_2_text: Sector, size, valuation—whatever you ask for. Companies that fail any rule are excluded, and we can tell you why: “It is worth $1.9B, and you asked for more than $2B.”
help_step_3_text: AI (Jev) scores every company once a month on four things: fundamentals, valuation, financing risk, and catalysts. Everyone gets the same scores; you decide how much each one counts.
help_step_3_extra: If you add your own question, AI answers it only for companies that pass your rules: yes or no, and with what confidence.
help_step_4_text: Your weights produce a score from 0 to 100 for each company. They are ranked, with market capitalization breaking ties. The top N are included, subject to your per-sector limit. Anything that does not fill the N slots stays in cash.
help_step_5_title: The portfolio is fixed and compared with the S&P 500
help_step_5_text: The portfolio is formed on the night of the last trading day. Until half an hour before the market opens on the first trading day you can swap and restore companies; after that it is fixed and does not change. It is compared with the S&P 500 over the same window: more than 0.2 points above earns 3 points; within 0.2 points earns 1; below earns 0.
help_by_ai: Scored by AI · the same for everyone
help_by_code: Handled by code · repeatable every time

help_model_item_3: The answer to your own question
help_model_note: It is always labeled as AI, and the scores are the same for every strategy.
help_code_item_2: Ranking, breaking ties, and sector limits
help_code_note: The same scores always produce the same result.

help_example_disclaimer: Fictional example · not a real company
help_example_reason: Included: fourth among the companies that pass your rules, within the limit of two companies per sector.
help_fairness_rules: Rules are versioned. Each strategy records which catalog version it played with.
help_fairness_results: Official results are never rewritten. They are fixed when the round closes and stay that way.
help_fairness_scores: Everyone's portfolio is fixed using the same scores. Official scores are generated on the afternoon of the last trading day and portfolios are formed that same night. Until half an hour before the market opens on day one you can only swap and restore companies, without AI, and no one knows that day's market move when the portfolio is fixed.
help_fairness_house: The house is scored just like you. Alpha, Omega, and Lambda play in the same round, against the same S&P and with the same points; their portfolios come from system methods and are not published.
help_question_text: In your strategy, “Why isn't X included?” tells you whether a company would be included and why. If it still does not add up, write to us.
help_disclaimer: Vennett compares paper strategies: no real money is involved, and this is not financial advice.
